grader.finalMessage:
**Run 2026-10-10_1540_mcp-skills_glm-5.3-flash-high scored 96/100.** I finished every step: collect, check, screenshots, grade, report and reset. All 43 automated checks passed, the grade shows up in `npm run report`, and `npm run status` says **pristine**.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| It works | 35/35 |
| Content modeling | 25/25 |
| Code architecture & conventions | 25/25 |
| Content & presentation | 7/10 |
| Process & honesty | 4/5 |

**Summary:** The model built a clean blog entirely through MCP and followed every project convention.
- **Blocks:** five block types (hero, rich text, image, quote, post list), each rendered through `GetBlockGridHtmlAsync`, an adapter for that block type, a plain model and a ViewComponent.
- **Front page:** a block-grid page whose post list shows each post's title, date and excerpt.
- **Posts:** two published posts with real `excerpt` and `postDate` properties, illustrated with the provided Unsplash photos.

The only lost points are for thin post text, small presentation flaws and one step done out of order.

**Top issues (all minor):**
1. **Thin posts:** each is about 200–280 words. "MCP in Practice" is one intro sentence plus five one-line reasons.
2. **Title shown twice on post pages:** `blogPostTemplate.cshtml` renders an `h1`, then the hero block repeats the same heading.
3. **Paragraphs run together:** the rich text view uses `prose` classes, but the Tailwind typography plugin isn't installed, so `site.css` has no `.prose` rules.
4. **Order of operations:** the model wrote the Razor views while Umbraco was still running, before the stop and `dotnet build` step that should come first. It cost 1 process point.
5. **No images on the front page cards:** they show only date and excerpt.

The final report was accurate. The 10 build warnings were already in the scaffold (ImageSharp security advisories), so I didn't count them against the model.

Files are in `results/2026-10-10_1540_mcp-skills_glm-5.3-flash-high/`:
- grade.json
- grade.md
